summary: The change makes S256 PKCE mandatory on both browser authorization entry points, stores the challenge with each code, verifies the hashed verifier before consuming a code, leaves codes intact on failed attempts, and updates tests and documentation.

evidence: src/passport.ts:2249-2265 and src/passport.ts:1093-1103 require a 43-character S256 code challenge and method on both /authorize and /api/auth/sso/authorize, then store the challenge with the issued code.

src/passport.ts:1148-1160 hashes the exchange verifier and passes a predicate to consumeSsoCode that compares the stored challenge plus client, audience, origin, and redirect metadata before deletion.
src/auth_store.ts:995-1016 returns without deleting the code when the verifier/metadata predicate fails, so missing, malformed, plain, and mismatched attempts do not consume valid codes.
src/handler_test.ts:2483-2557 and tests/worker_runtime.mjs:815-890 cover successful S256 exchange and missing, malformed, plain, and mismatched rejection cases.
